text:
maya: Heads-up — we got a p99 spike for chat-api starting ~01:10 UTC after last night's runtime deploy. Metrics: p95 ~120ms (ok) p99 ~980ms (up from ~240ms). dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/abc123

devon: copying the dashboard. any recent kernel/attention changes in the deploy?

ops-bot: deploy finished: runtime@release-2026-03-17 (commit 9f3b2d). Canary 5% -> success.

maya: yes, the deploy included SDPA heuristic tuning + flashattn compileflag tweak (-O3 -> -Ofast) per PR #412.

rik: can we confirm kernel selection logs for affected requests? `logs.query("kernel_select", service="runtime", since=01:00)` might show misroutes to SDPA for short chats.

maya: pulled a sample trace for a slow request:
```
kernel_select: model=gpt-small, seq=64 -> selected=sdpa_f32
latency_breakdown: kernel_exec=920ms, queue=10ms
kv_cache_miss=true
```
Looks like SDPA kernel executed for seq=64 (should prefer flashattn).

devon: weird — SDPA should have lower cost on some hwmap but not 4x latency. maybe compileflag made flashattn worse. QA: can you repro locally?

qa-jen: I can repro in staging with a quick load: `wrk -t2 -c20 -d20s https://staging-api.redwood/chat?model=gpt-small` p99 ~900ms. I'll attach perf flamegraphs. Ticket: CS-8912 (customer complaining).

maya: temporary mitigation: toggled kernel priority to prefer flashattn for gpt-small on affected pool and restarted workers in canary. Command used:
```
rdctl runtime set-kernel-priority --model gpt-small --pool canary --priority flashattn,sdpa
```

devon: also toggle SDPA heuristic off for canary so it won't be auto-selected:
```
rdctl runtime set-heuristic --name sdpa_autoselect --value false --env canary
```

ops-bot: action: kernel-priority update applied to 3 canary machines; heuristic flag set.

maya: after the changes p99 dropped to ~250ms on canary within 3 minutes. rolling to 20% now.

rik: good. we should bisect the changeset to see whether the compileflag or a kernel build is root cause. Steps I propose:
- revert compileflag on a canary worker and run regression test
- if repro goes away, revert flag globally and rebuild flashattn with previous flags
- otherwise bisect runtime commits between last-green and 9f3b2d

devon: agree. @qa-jen can you run the revert-flash compile locally with this command and report p99?
```
make -C runtime/modules/flashattn clean && \
CFLAGS="-O3 -march=znver2" make -C runtime/modules/flashattn build && 
./tests/perf_flashattn --seq 64 --batch 8
```

qa-jen: started the build, will post numbers in ~12m.

support-bot: linked CS-8912 -> internal thread 1729456789 for tracking. Customer notes: spike began 2026-03-17 01:12 UTC, affects ~10% of requests.

maya: temporary rollout notes: we prefer flashattn on the path until root cause found. please add an automated canary check that runs `wrk` against sample prompts after kernel/prio changes.

devon: adding canary test in CI: `tests/canary/latency_smoke.sh` will run basic p95/p99 thresholds post-deploy. PR coming.

qa-jen: build results: with compileflag revert p99 in staging is ~260ms. Rebuild that reverted flag back to -Ofast and p99 jumps to ~920ms. So compileflag is the culprit.

rik: great catch. we should roll the compileflag back in prod and do a more conservative optimization profile. Action items:
- revert compileflag in runtime build scripts (devon)
- schedule a rebuild and deploy (ops)
- add unit/perf test for flashattn seq=64 in CI (qa)
- postmortem draft (maya)

devon: opening PR to revert -Ofast -> -O3 for flashattn module (PR #427). tagging for urgent review.

ops-bot: prod rollback scheduled: runtime@release-2026-03-17-rollback (ETA 15m) by ops team.

maya: after rollback to previous build p99 back to baseline (~240ms). closing the immediate customer loop. :thumbsup:

qa-jen: will add perf test and a perf gate so -Ofast cannot land without CI perf pass.

support-bot: updated CS-8912: mitigation applied and customer notified.

maya: postmortem will include root cause (aggressive compileflag causing suboptimal codegen for flashattn on our HW), mitigation (revert + perf gate), and follow-ups (kernel-selection hardening). I'll start the draft.

devon: thanks all. next: add a tiny canary job that asserts p99 < 400ms for seq=64 after any kernel-related change.

rik: also add a telemetry alert for sudden kernel-exec dominated latency where kernel_exec > 70% of total for p99.

maya: noted. closing thread when postmortem is uploaded.
